summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for acute gastroenteritis and decompensated diastolic heart failure, presenting with vomiting, diarrhea, and worsening shortness of breath. She was treated with IV furosemide for fluid overload, resulting in improved respiratory status and resolution of pulmonary crackles. Her diarrhea resolved and was determined to be likely viral, with negative stool studies. Cardiac workup revealed no acute coronary syndrome or pulmonary embolism; chest pain was attributed to heart failure and gastroesophageal causes. An enlarged pulmonary artery suggested pulmonary hypertension. Her chronic osteomyelitis and recent ORIF were stable, with healing fractures and continued antibiotic therapy. She was discharged home on increased diuretic dosing, with follow-up planned for heart, transplant, and orthopedic care.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Intestinal infection due to other organism, not elsewhere classified
Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
